instruction: Use Abaqus to build and solve a 2D axisymmetric finite-element model of a circular plate. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 2D axisymmetric deformable solid part representing the circular plate cross-section. The radial extent is from r = 0 mm to r = 50 mm. The axial/thickness extent is from z = 0 mm to z = 1 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3. Assign this material to the entire plate using a homogeneous solid section. Discretization: Mesh the part with CAX4R axisymmetric solid elements using a structured technique. Apply a radial seed size of 2.0 mm with one element through the thickness. Create node sets named AXIS (r = 0 boundary), OUTER (r = 50 mm boundary), and TOP (z = 1 mm boundary). Boundary Conditions: Constrain the radial displacement U1 = 0 on the AXIS node set. On the OUTER node set, constrain both U1 = 0 and U2 = 0. Loading: Apply a downward pressure of 0.1 N/mm² on the TOP boundary by representing it as equivalent axisymmetric concentrated nodal forces. For each top node at radius r_i, calculate the force in the U2 direction using: F_i = -p × 2πr_i × Δr_i For the first and last top nodes, use half the adjacent radial interval for Δr_i. For interior top nodes, use half the distance between neighboring top nodes. The node at r = 0 receives zero equivalent force. Analysis Step: Create a static analysis step named Step-Pressure. Request field output for displacement U, reaction force RF, and stress S. Job Execution: Create and submit a job named Job-Plate. Wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: Save the model database as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Plate.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Plate.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.

instruction: Use Abaqus to build and solve a 2D axisymmetric finite-element model of an internally pressurized thick-walled cylinder. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 2D axisymmetric deformable solid part representing the cylinder cross-section. The radial extent is from r = 50 mm to r = 100 mm. The axial extent is from z = 0 mm to z = 10 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Assign this material to the entire cylinder using a homogeneous solid section. Discretization: Mesh the part with CAX4R axisymmetric solid elements using a structured technique. Apply a global seed size of 5.0 mm. Create node sets named ALLNODES (all nodes), INNER (r = 50 mm boundary), OUTER (r = 100 mm boundary), ZMIN (z = 0 mm boundary), and ZMAX (z = 10 mm boundary). Boundary Conditions: Constrain the axial displacement U2 = 0 on the ALLNODES set to enforce the plane-strain condition. Do not apply any additional radial U1 constraint. Loading: Apply an internal pressure of p = 10 N/mm^2 on the INNER boundary (r = 50 mm) by representing it as equivalent axisymmetric concentrated nodal forces. For each INNER node at axial position z_i, calculate the force in the positive U1 direction using: F_i = p x 2pi x r_in x Delta z_i where r_in = 50 mm. For the first and last INNER nodes, use half the adjacent axial interval for Delta z_i. For interior INNER nodes, use half the distance between neighboring INNER nodes. Analysis Step: Create a static analysis step named Step-Pressure. Request field output for displacement U, reaction force RF, and stress S. Job Execution: Create and submit a job named Job-Cylinder. Wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: Save the model database as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Cylinder.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Cylinder.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.

instruction: Use Abaqus to perform a tensile analysis of a thin rectangular shell plate with a central circular hole. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Build a 3D Deformable Shell part consisting of a 120 mm by 240 mm rectangular plate on the XY plane with a central 12 mm diameter circular hole centered at (60, 120) mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Homogeneous Shell Section with a thickness of 1 mm and 5 through-thickness integration points, and assign it to the entire plate. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the shell plate. Analysis Step: Define a Static, General step named Step-HoleTension with the Initial step as its predecessor. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply opposing tensile shell edge loads of 8 N/mm to the vertical edges: on the left edge at X = 0 in the negative X direction, and on the right edge at X = 120 in the positive X direction. Constrain the plate to prevent rigid-body motion without over-constraining the tensile deformation: - Fix U1 = U2 = U3 = 0 at the bottom-left corner (0, 0). - Fix U2 = U3 = 0 at the bottom-right corner (120, 0). - Fix U3 = 0 at the top-left corner (0, 240). Discretization: Mesh the plate using S4R shell elements. Apply a local seed size of approximately 2.4 mm to the hole edge and a global seed size of 10 mm to the remainder of the plate. Job Execution: Create and submit a job named Job-FlangeHole. Wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: Save the model database to C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-FlangeHole.cae and ensure the output database is written to C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-FlangeHole.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.

instruction: Use Abaqus to complete the following task. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Build a straight rectangular bar with length 100 mm along the global X-axis. The cross-section is a 10 mm x 10 mm square in the Y-Z plane, so the final geometry occupies X = 0 to 100 mm, Y = 0 to 10 mm, and Z = 0 to 10 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Steel and assign it to the entire bar. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the bar. Analysis Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-Load, placed after the Initial step. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply an Encastre boundary condition to the end face at X = 0. Apply a tensile Surface Traction, General to the end face at X = 100 mm. Set the traction magnitude to 10 MPa acting in the global positive X direction. This traction is equivalent to a total tensile force of 1000 N distributed over the 10 mm x 10 mm end face. Discretization: Mesh the bar with a global seed size of 5 mm. Assign the element type C3D8R and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-Tension, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Post-Processing: Open the output database. Display the Mises stress contour. Query the U1 displacement at the node located at the center of the free end face (X = 100 mm, Y = 5 mm, Z = 5 mm). instruction: Use Abaqus to perform a steady-state heat conduction analysis in a consistent millimeter-based unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (100, 50) in the X-Y plane and extrude along the global Z-axis to a thickness of 10 mm. This produces a plate with in-plane dimensions 100 mm x 50 mm and thickness 10 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Copper with thermal conductivity = 0.0004 W/(mm·K), equivalent to 400 W/(m·K). Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Copper and assign it to the entire plate. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the plate. Analysis Step: Create a Heat Transfer, Steady-state step named Step-Thermal. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply a temperature of 100 degC to the end face at X = 0 (the face with normal in -X, dimensions 50 mm x 10 mm). Apply a temperature of 20 degC to the end face at X = 100 mm (the face with normal in +X, dimensions 50 mm x 10 mm). Keep all other faces adiabatic by applying no thermal boundary condition to them. Discretization: Mesh the plate with a global seed size of 5 mm. Assign the element type DC3D8 and generate the mesh. instruction: Use Abaqus/CAE to complete the provided block-on-plate nonlinear contact seed model in the N-mm-MPa unit system. Start from C:\Users\user\Desktop\Contact-Seed.cae; do not rebuild or replace its preloaded geometry, material, section, assembly, named surfaces, or named sets. The seed contains an unmeshed 10 mm x 10 mm x 12 mm 3D deformable Block, an unmeshed 30 mm x 30 mm x 4 mm 3D deformable Plate, Steel with E = 210000 MPa and nu = 0.3, the Steel-Solid homogeneous solid section assigned to both parts, and dependent instances with BLOCK-1 centered on PLATE-1: block X/Y = 10..20 mm and Z = 4..16 mm, plate X/Y = 0..30 mm and Z = 0..4 mm. Preserve the named regions SURF_BLOCK_TOP, SURF_BLOCK_BOTTOM, SURF_PLATE_TOP, SET_PLATE_BOTTOM, SET_BLOCK_GUIDE_A, and SET_BLOCK_GUIDE_B. Analysis: create a Static, General step named Step-Contact after Initial with Nlgeom = ON, initial increment 0.05, maximum increment 0.1, minimum increment 1e-8, and at most 200 increments. Contact: create one finite-sliding Surface-to-Surface Contact (Standard) interaction active in Initial, using SURF_PLATE_TOP as the main surface and SURF_BLOCK_BOTTOM as the secondary surface; use one interaction property with Hard normal contact, separation allowed, and frictionless tangential behavior. Boundary conditions: apply ENCASTRE to SET_PLATE_BOTTOM; to remove only the block's frictionless in-plane rigid-body modes, set U1 = U2 = 0 on SET_BLOCK_GUIDE_A and U2 = 0 on SET_BLOCK_GUIDE_B, leaving U3 unconstrained on both guide sets. Load: in Step-Contact apply a uniform positive pressure of 5 MPa to SURF_BLOCK_TOP, acting inward/downward; the 100 mm2 loaded area gives a 500 N resultant. Mesh: use structured HEX C3D8R elements, a 2 mm global seed on Block, and a 3 mm global seed on Plate; generate both meshes. Output: request U, S, RF, and contact stress output so the solved ODB contains CPRESS for the required contact pair. Job and deliverables: create and submit Job-Contact, wait for successful completion, verify nonzero displacement, Mises stress, and CPRESS results and pressure/reaction equilibrium, then save the completed database as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Contact.cae with the solved output database at C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-Contact.odb.

Task 08 was therefore redesigned as a provided, incomplete 10 x 10 x 12 mm block-on-30 x 30 x 4 mm plate seed that preserves the nonlinear contact learning objective while producing a native 494-node solved model within the licensed limit.

instruction: Use Abaqus to perform a simply supported beam analysis under a uniformly distributed load. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a 10 mm x 10 mm rectangle in the Y-Z plane and extrude along the global X-axis to a length of 200 mm. This produces a beam with cross-section 10 mm x 10 mm and span 200 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Steel and assign it to the entire beam. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the beam. Analysis Step: Create a Static, General step named Step-Load. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Create a reference point RP-1 at the geometric center of the left end face (X = 0, Y = 5 mm, Z = 5 mm) and couple it kinematically to that end face. Create a reference point RP-2 at the geometric center of the right end face (X = 200 mm, Y = 5 mm, Z = 5 mm) and couple it kinematically to that end face. At RP-1, constrain U1 = U2 = U3 = 0 and UR2 = UR3 = 0 to model a pinned support that allows rotation about the beam axis (UR1). At RP-2, constrain U2 = U3 = 0 and UR2 = UR3 = 0 to model a roller support that allows axial motion (U1) and rotation about the beam axis (UR1). Apply a pressure of 0.05 MPa downward on the beam top surface (Y = 10 mm face). This loading is equivalent to a uniformly distributed load q = 0.5 N/mm. Discretization: Mesh the beam with a global seed size of 5 mm. Assign the element type C3D8R and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-UDL, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: Save the model database as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-UDL.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-UDL.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.
